the use of Internet-based smoking cessation interventions among racial/ethnic minority smokers and smokers with low income.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the psychometric properties (internal consistency and test-re-test reliability) of Internet-administering measures commonly used in cessation trials among racial/ ethnic minorities and smokers with low income were satisfactory to excellent.
the Internet-based measures are reliable in all strata except for the quit methods.
the psychometric properties for the majority of the measures examined are not affected by race/ethnic minority status or income.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reliability of Internet-administering measures of smoking behavior and psychosocial factors is good in a diverse sample of smokers.
we found no evidence that Internet-administered questionnaires are less reliable than telephone-administered questionaires in a diverse sample of smokers.
the psychometric properties for most of the Internet-administered questionnaires we examined were similar across race/ethnicity strata and across income strata.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Internet-administered instruments can be reliably administered in a diverse sample of smokers, which will allow us to conduct more rigorous Web-based cessation research in priority groups.
Internet-administered questionnaires can be used to measure psychosocial constructs in a reliable way in a diverse sample of smokers.
Internet-based measures are psychometrically sound in diverse populations.
